_comment: PINNED ceyx native-decoder release consumed by scripts/build_apps.py.
The tag fixes WHICH GitHub release the Linux/Windows prebuilt libraries come
from; the per-asset sha256 fixes WHICH BYTES, because a tag can be moved and
an asset re-uploaded. build_apps.py downloads the asset directly by tag (no
GitHub API call, so anonymous rate limits cannot fail a pinned build) and
refuses to place a library whose sha256 does not match.
This file is edited by hand OR, deliberately, by
`python3 scripts/build_apps.py --ceyx-release latest`, which resolves the
newest release, downloads its assets, records their real digests here, and
STOPS without building. The maintainer then reviews this diff and commits it.
An upstream release therefore cannot alter Halcyon's decoder without a
visible, reviewable change to this file.
sha256 provenance: computed on 2026-08-28 by downloading each asset from
https://github.com/jhangyu/ceyx/releases/download/v0.1.1/<asset> and running
`shasum -a 256`. Trust-on-first-use (same authority that serves the bytes):
catches any FUTURE substitution, not one predating this date.
macOS is intentionally ABSENT: its plugin vendors six interdependent dylibs
(decoder + lcms2 + jpeg + heif + de265 + omp) with install-name/codesign
wiring the single-decoder release asset cannot satisfy. macOS keeps its
committed libraries. Android is out of scope for this pin.
